Comuna 13 is a neighborhood in Medellín that visitors explore on a city walk. The walls of its buildings are covered with graffiti and murals by local artists. Through imagery and storytelling, the artwork recounts important events in the neighborhood's history, the lives of its residents and their hopes for the future.

A walk here offers a chance to experience street art in its urban setting. Comuna 13 is included in Medellín sightseeing tours alongside squares, parks and works by Fernando Botero. The stops and duration of each excursion depend on the chosen itinerary.

## The Colorful Town on the Route of Flowers

Ataco's full name is Concepción de Ataco. The town lies in the mountainous part of Ahuachapán Department and is on the [Route of Flowers](/el-salvador/place/ruta-de-las-flores/). It's a pleasure to wander its cobbled streets, admire the painted façades and visit small craft workshops.

Murals have become one of Ataco's most recognizable features. Bright scenes painted on walls stand alongside tiled roofs, flowers and the everyday life of a small Salvadoran town.

## Textiles, Coffee and Cuisine

Ataco is known for its weaving traditions. Discovering locally made textiles adds another dimension to a walk through the center and offers a glimpse of how artisans keep traditional skills alive in their daily work.

Coffee grows on the surrounding hillsides. A farm visit or an introduction to coffee processing can be arranged as a separate experience, while in town you can stop at a café. Local food and culinary events add to a journey through western El Salvador.

## Ataco on an Itinerary

On the [Best of El Salvador](/el-salvador/tour/el-salvador-san-salvador-suchitoto-gulf-of-fonseca/) tour, Ataco is visited on day three, after the archaeological sites of Chalchuapa and Santa Ana. The itinerary highlights textiles and murals; a dedicated coffee tour can be arranged separately.

At Concha y Toro, an introduction to Chile begins among rows of vines and on a stroll through the estate gardens. Pirque lies in the Maipo Valley near Santiago: after the city streets, the green gardens and mountains beyond the vineyards are especially welcome. The wine in your glass has a landscape you can see all around you.

The visitor center introduces the winery's history, old estate and different aspects of wine production. One of the best-known parts of the tour is the Casillero del Diablo cellar. The legend of a devil said to have frightened away wine thieves has become part of the brand's story. The visit connects names on wine labels to a real place, while a tasting introduces selected wines produced by the estate.

On an Ada Tours wine journey, Concha y Toro complements visits to Argentine wineries and the Chilean capital. It is a convenient place for a day devoted to wine before returning to Santiago. The visitor center offers several tour options: the route around the grounds, number of wines tasted and additional culinary experiences depend on the booking. The precise inclusions are confirmed in the tour itinerary.

At Confluencia, the mountains occupy almost the entire horizon. Tents stand on the rocky valley floor, slopes in shades of ochre and gray rise all around, and high white peaks are visible in the distance. After the approach hike, it feels especially good to take off your backpack, pour a hot drink and look back along the trail. This is where travelers begin to experience life on an Andean expedition.

Confluencia is in Aconcagua Provincial Park, on the approach through the Horcones Valley from the Mendoza area. It is the first camp on the way to Plaza de Mulas and a stopping point on some trekking itineraries. At over 3,000 meters in elevation, even a technically straightforward hike calls for an unhurried pace. The rocky trail, exposed sunshine and changing weather shape the experience.

On the Ada Tours Aconcagua expedition, participants arrive here after their permits have been checked at the park entrance. Mules carry part of the load on the approach; an overnight stay and an acclimatization hike toward Plaza Francia follow. Meals, tents and baggage transport are specified in each itinerary. For a day visit or overnight stay, the trip plan and park access should be arranged in advance, taking the season and participants' experience into account.
